title: Cohomological bounds for a complete complex from residue Tor amplitude
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and residue field $k=R/(\varpi)$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], meaning that every open cover has a finite subcover, with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\varpi^n)_X$, the inverse limit of the constant quotient ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] be derived complete for its quotient tower, meaning that the quotient maps exhibit $K$ as a derived limit of $(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(R/\varpi^n)_X)_{n\geq1}$, with its canonical reduction transitions and all terms viewed in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ by restriction of scalars [def-weil-derived-limit, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Suppose there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $K_1=K\otimes^L_{B_X}k_X$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: for every site object $V\to X$ and every sheaf $N$ of $k_V$-modules, $H^j((K_1|_V)\otimes^L_{k_V}N)=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-tensor, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Then $H^j(K)=0$ for every $j\notin[a,b]$. No constructibility or local constancy of the residue cohomology is required.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof of (1) and (2): these two arguments use completeness and finite residue Tor amplitude, not constructibility; Tag 099Q, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, and sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles. Transfer from constant to completed coefficients by algebraization.tex Tag 099I, lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence.

proof.text: Write $C_n=(R/\varpi^n)_X$ with its $B_X$-module structure given by the $n$-th projection, and $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_X}C_n$, viewed over $B_X$ by restriction of scalars. In the Tor-amplitude hypothesis take $V=X$ and $N=k_X$. The unit identity $K_1\otimes^L_{k_X}k_X\cong K_1$ follows on a K-flat representative from $P\otimes_{k_X}k_X=P$. Hence $H^j(K_1)=0$ outside $[a,b]$. This is just the defining test of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], with derived tensor as in [def-weil-derived-tensor].

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude: test against the coefficient sheaf itself

proof.text: Choose a representative of $K$ and a single K-flat resolution $P^\bullet$ with flat $B_X$-module terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For every $n\geq1$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] identifies $P_n^\bullet=P^\bullet\otimes_{B_X}C_n$ with $K_n$. Use the actual chain maps $1_P\otimes(C_{n+1}\to C_n)$ as its strict transition maps. These are the canonical quotient transitions in the completeness hypothesis, because the same resolution computes every reduction and every quotient map.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change (identity underlying topos)

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$ the coefficient sequence $0\to k_X\xrightarrow{u_n}C_{n+1}\to C_n\to0$, where $u_n(\bar r)=\varpi^n r\bmod\varpi^{n+1}$, is short exact as a sequence of $B_X$-modules. Indeed, $R$ is a DVR with nonzero uniformizer by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]: cancellation of $\varpi^n$ shows that $u_n$ is well defined and injective, and its image is exactly the kernel of the quotient map, which is surjective. By the constant-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], sections locally come from elements of the coefficient modules and equality can be checked after a covering refinement; therefore the same kernel calculation and local lifts prove exactness of the sheaf sequence. The maps are $B_X$-linear: for a local section $z$ of $B_X$, its components satisfy $z_{n+1}\bmod\varpi=z_1$, so $z_{n+1}\varpi^n r=\varpi^n z_1r$ modulo $\varpi^{n+1}$, checked locally where the finite coefficient sections are constant.

source.place: Tag 0942, lemma-bounded, proof: the coefficient ideal-quotient filtration, specialized to the principal DVR ideal

proof.text: Each $P^j$ is flat, so tensoring the short exact coefficient sequence of Step 3 with $P^j$ preserves exactness, precisely the definition in [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Thus $0\to P_1^\bullet\to P_{n+1}^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] in the abelian category of $B_X$-module sheaves to get the distinguished triangle $K_1\to K_{n+1}\to K_n\to K_1[1]$. Its second arrow is the canonical transition from Step 2, not an independently chosen isomorphism between reductions. By [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact], for every $j$ its cohomology sequence contains $H^j(K_1)\to H^j(K_{n+1})\to H^j(K_n)\to H^{j+1}(K_1)$.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor; Tag 05RS, cohomology of distinguished triangles

proof.text: Induct on $n\geq1$ to prove $H^j(K_n)=0$ for all $j\notin[a,b]$. The base $n=1$ is Step 1. For the induction step, the exact segment in Step 4 has $H^j(K_1)=H^j(K_n)=0$ for such $j$, forcing $H^j(K_{n+1})=0$. At $j=b$, its next term is $H^{b+1}(K_1)=0$, so the same segment proves that every canonical transition $H^b(K_{n+1})\to H^b(K_n)$ is an epimorphism. This proves both assertions for the entire fixed tower.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof of (1),(2): uniform bounds and surjectivity in the top degree; the DVR induction expands Tag 0942

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-milnor-sequence] to the strict tower $P_n^\bullet$ of $B_X$-module complexes on the small pro-etale site, with $T$ built from the termwise product complex $\prod_nP_n^\bullet$. It gives $0\to R^1\varprojlim_n H^{j-1}(K_n)\to H^j(R\varprojlim_n P_n^\bullet)\to\varprojlim_n H^j(K_n)\to0$ for every $j$, where $R\varprojlim_nP_n^\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]$; shifting the initial index from $0$ to $1$ only renames the tower. This cone is a derived limit of the tower $(K_n)$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ in the sense of [def-weil-derived-limit]. Indeed, by [det-pe-products-derived] the termwise product $\prod_nP_n^\bullet$, with the images of its termwise projections, is a product of the $K_n$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$; since the localization functor preserves composites and differences, $\mathrm{pr}_n\circ Q(1-T)=\mathrm{pr}_n-Q(t_n)\circ\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$, so $Q(1-T)$ is the transition endomorphism $1-s$ of the tower with its canonical transitions from Step 2. The cone triangle $\prod_nP_n^\bullet\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nP_n^\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)\to(\prod_nP_n^\bullet)[1]$ is distinguished by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and since (TR2) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] is an equivalence, the triangle $\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1]\xrightarrow{-\delta[-1]}\prod_nP_n^\bullet\xrightarrow{1-T}\prod_nP_n^\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)$, whose rotation is the cone triangle (with $\delta$ its third arrow), is distinguished; it is a Roos triangle. Completeness supplies $K$ as a derived limit of this same canonical tower. By clause 1 of [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], any two derived limits of a fixed tower are isomorphic; hence $H^j(K)\cong H^j(\operatorname{Cone}(1-T)[-1])$, the Milnor middle term. No canonical choice of that isomorphism is needed for vanishing.

source.place: Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, (5) and (7); derived.tex Tag 08TC, definition-derived-limit and following uniqueness discussion

proof.text: For $j<a$ both towers in the outer terms of the Milnor sequence are zero by Step 5, as are both towers for $j>b+1$. Their limits and first derived limits are zero (equivalently their defining product kernels and cokernels are zero). At the remaining degree $j=b+1$, the right-hand tower is zero, and the left-hand term is $R^1\varprojlim_n H^b(K_n)$. The transitions of this latter tower are epimorphisms by Step 5, so [det-pe-milnor-epimorphic], applied with ring sheaf $\mathcal R=B_X$, makes that term zero as well. Exactness therefore gives $H^j(K)=0$ in every degree outside $[a,b]$.

split_report.summary: Expanded the residue-to-complete cohomology argument over the actual completed coefficient sheaf. A single flat-term K-flat resolution makes the canonical reduction transitions explicit; the DVR quotient short exact sequences give the uniform cohomology interval and surjective top cohomology transitions by induction, and the existing pro-etale Milnor statements remove the possible b+1 term. Statement unchanged; no constructibility, invertibility or local constancy added, and no new nodes required. The assignment file was recovered read-only from the synchronized live DAG mirror because the shared checkout lacked it.
split_report.blueprint: Supports the local projective-model induction below lem-fix-weil-operations, proof paragraph beginning "For an admissible exceptional adjoint", sentence "Evaluation is natural in the two Weil maps and their inverses, so its square commutes", through lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion and lem-fix-residue-lisse-projective-models. Realizes the latter split's use of this item for the cohomology interval in its residue-basis induction.

tool_uses.why: A flat-term K-flat representative on an arbitrary ringed site makes every canonical reduction a strict complex; this unit has no resolution theorem.
Computes derived reduction over the nonconstant completed coefficient sheaf using the same K-flat representative; this unit has no ambient change-of-rings theorem.
Converts the explicit degreewise short exact sequence into a triangle in any abelian derived category; this is a generic homological tool, not an alternative projection-formula route.
Supplies exactness of the cohomology sequence of the displayed triangle in an arbitrary abelian derived category; no node in the unit states it.
Supplies the sheaf Milnor sequence for arbitrary ring sheaves on the pro-etale site, including B_X; this is the limit calculation called for by Stacks 09C2.
Only clause 1, uniqueness up to noncanonical isomorphism, identifies the hypothesized derived limit with the explicit cone model used by the Milnor statement.
Kills the first derived limit of the already proved epimorphic top-cohomology tower; this is the pro-etale limit tool needed by the source route.

Only the statement that termwise products of complexes of B_X-modules on the pro-etale site are products in the derived category, needed to see the Milnor cone Cone(1-T)[-1] as a derived limit in the sense of def-weil-derived-limit; this unit has no product theorem.
